subject.title: [Bug]: iOS app fails to connect over Tailscale CGNAT (100.x.x.x) — wss:// required but WebSocket upgrade silently dropped

question: What iOS remote/Tailscale connection policy should OpenClaw support for first-time mobile Gateway pairing?
rationale: The remaining work crosses TLS/fingerprint trust, Tailscale Serve versus direct CGNAT behavior, and mobile setup-code auth, so automation should not decide whether to keep fail-closed behavior, add native TLS trust UX, or allow plaintext tailnet exceptions.

options.title: Keep Raw Tailnet Fail-Closed
options.body: Require Tailscale Serve/Funnel or another real wss:// endpoint, then improve iOS diagnostics, route probing, and fingerprint/setup flow so users can complete that secure path.

options.title: Support Native Gateway TLS Over Tailnet
options.body: Add and document a first-class native Gateway TLS/fingerprint trust flow for direct tailnet hosts, with live iOS proof and compatibility checks for existing CLI/local workflows.

options.title: Allow Raw Tailnet ws:// Explicitly
options.body: Treat 100.64.0.0/10 and .ts.net as approved plaintext-local routes only if maintainers accept the weaker mobile security boundary and update tests/docs accordingly.

recommendation.title: Keep Raw Tailnet Fail-Closed
recommendation.body: Require Tailscale Serve/Funnel or another real wss:// endpoint, then improve iOS diagnostics, route probing, and fingerprint/setup flow so users can complete that secure path.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the recent Tailnet route-list fix and is closest in current history to the Serve/mobile pairing policy and docs direction.
